subject: imposing truncated priors on elements of a parameter vector

messages.author: 68021dbcedde29d4
messages.subject: imposing truncated priors on elements of a parameter vector
parts:
In the hierarchical regression example in the manual on page 70, is there a way to impose a truncated prior or distribution on a single element in the beta matrix?  For example, say I have an intercept and a single continuous independent variable.  Essentially, the transformed parameters matrix declaration becomes:

matrix[J,2] beta;  -- a 2 column matrix.

What I am wondering if there is a way to keep the 1st column freely estimated, but constrain the 2nd parameter to have a lower value of zero.  I wish to keep the generalarity of the matrix notation but allow element of that matric to be drawn from truncated distributions.  E.g., real <lower=0> beta[J,2]

Is there any trick to doing this or should I simply create two vectors (2 being my example) where they are defined as

vector[J] beta1
vector<lower=0>[J] beta2

... etc if I have more than two variables...

Thanks,

Tom Eagle

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] imposing truncated priors on elements of a parameter vector
parts:
There's no way to constrain only part of a
variable. So you need to define the two vectors
separately (as you show how to do). The best
way to put them together is then:

matrix[J,2] beta;
beta <- append_col(beta1,beta2);

The copying's not so expensive relative to gradient
calcs, but no need to build up beta if you don't need
it.

And you probably want beta to be a local variable
rather than transformed parameter so that you don't
see it in the output (unless you're going to need it
in more than the block where it's defined).

- Bob
